scope: City-owned park; not County expenditure or household assistance

sources.title: City of Pueblo — Mountain Park recovery

sections.title: Scope
sections.finding: City park recovery in Beulah; separate from county emergency expenses and household aid.

sections.title: Fire chronology
sections.finding: The City dates the fire onset to June 29, 2026.

sections.title: Physical loss
sections.finding: Fire and subsequent floods damaged buildings, roads and trails; surviving structures require assessment.

sections.title: Public access
sections.finding: City reports the park remains closed; this report cannot authorize entry.

sections.title: Area
sections.finding: CPR describes the park as approximately 600 acres, not a measured burn footprint.

sections.title: Public meetings
sections.finding: The City identifies October 20 in Beulah and October 22 in Pueblo as its two initial meetings.

sections.title: Public communication
sections.finding: Use the City's recovery portal to follow new meeting announcements and recovery plans.

sections.title: Education continuity
sections.finding: CPR reports nonprofit programs shifted to the River Campus; verify service counts separately.

sections.title: Children and families
sections.finding: Compare delivered sessions, transportation costs and accessibility; avoid individual child records.

sections.title: Equitable access
sections.finding: Record barriers for older adults, disabled visitors and households without vehicles; no distributional result yet.

sections.title: Ownership
sections.finding: CPR identifies the park as City-owned; verify title and operating agreements for precise rights.

sections.title: Municipal leadership
sections.finding: Parks and Recreation is leading public recovery communication; detailed delegations are not established here.

sections.title: State role
sections.finding: The state recipient and municipal applicant have distinct grant responsibilities; confirm award terms.

sections.title: FEMA authority
sections.finding: Damage documentation and grant eligibility are distinct from local authority to rebuild.

sections.title: Insurance provider
sections.finding: The City identifies CIRSA as its self-insurance provider; settlement documentation is not available here.

sections.title: Insurance range
sections.finding: CPR reports expected insurance proceeds of $4.9–6.3 million; this is not verified receipt or total project cost.

sections.title: Reporting clock
sections.finding: FEMA guidance allows 60 days from the recovery scoping meeting to identify disaster impacts, with possible extensions.

sections.title: Deadline uncertainty
sections.finding: City reports FEMA meetings began early October; exact triggering date, extension and submission status are not established.

sections.title: Grant stages
sections.finding: Track application, eligibility, obligation, disbursement and reimbursement separately; park-specific award unverified.

sections.title: Funding separation
sections.finding: County disaster assistance and City insurance are different scopes; avoid double counting overlapping recovery funding.

sections.title: Net recovery cost
sections.finding: For each scope, compare eligible cost with applicable nonoverlapping funding; unknown values stay null.

sections.title: Cash reconciliation
sections.finding: Maintain separate ledgers for estimated, received, authorized, contracted, invoiced and paid amounts.

sections.title: Debris
sections.finding: CPR reports building debris remains; verify disposal scope and hazard assessment before work.

sections.title: Equipment
sections.finding: CPR reports damaged equipment was identified and removed; replacement costs remain unverified.

sections.title: Hazardous trees
sections.finding: Burn-damaged trees require professional assessment and clearance before access.

sections.title: Flooding and watershed
sections.finding: Evaluate post-fire runoff, debris flows and drainage before reopening vulnerable areas.

sections.title: Soil and revegetation
sections.finding: Track stabilized acreage and plant survival; do not invent treatment targets or completion figures.

sections.title: Roads and trails
sections.finding: Use inspection-based segment inventory; evaluate safe phased access rather than promise a reopening.

sections.title: Utilities
sections.finding: CPR identifies utility repairs among recovery needs; verify asset owners and inspections.

sections.title: Horseshoe Lodge
sections.finding: The City describes extensive lodge damage; surviving fabric and structural feasibility require qualified review.

sections.title: Heritage options
sections.finding: Compare stabilization, rehabilitation and reconstruction with preservation specialists before committing.

sections.title: Procurement
sections.finding: CPR reports consultants are being sought; verify solicitation, executed contracts and amendments.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.finding: Compare stabilization-only, phased reopening and broader rebuild with safety, cost and public benefit metrics.

sections.title: Decision gates
sections.finding: Require professional hazard clearance, applicable preservation review and funding authorization.

sections.title: Community participation
sections.finding: Publish meeting feedback themes and documented responses; do not assume consensus.

sections.title: Risk
sections.finding: Funding uncertainty, flooding, unsafe access and irreversible heritage loss are risks, not established future failures.

sections.title: Performance
sections.finding: Measure assessed assets, inspected trail segments, funded scopes and restored programs with dated denominators.

sections.title: Twin candidate
sections.finding: Candidate layers: public assets, watershed, closures, fiscal stages and education continuity; no operational activation.

sections.title: Evidence responsibility
sections.finding: Entities and users obtain underlying records; Q evaluates supplied and publicly available evidence. No records request sent.

sections.title: Lifecycle and correction
sections.finding: Recheck November 25 or upon official funding, meeting, hazard or scope change; retain prior versions.
